newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X shares tumble after weekend reports.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X shares tumble after weekend reports.

text.p: Shares in Canadian gold prospector Bre-X Minerals Ltd. tumbled on Monday as skittish investors sifted through the latest rumors and reports swirling around the Busang gold saga.

More than 15 million Bre-X shares changed hands on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Monday after a report by an Australian metallurgical firm, which cast further doubt on Busang, heralded by Bre-X as the gold find of the century.
The rumor mill was also fueled by unconfirmed reports that unidentified parties had been amassing Bre-X shares in preparation for a possible hostile takeover bid.
Bre-X finished a hectic Monday session down C66 cents to close at C$2.52 in Toronto, but recovered from a session low of C$2.26. Traders attributed the heavy volume to institutional selling.
"All this stuff just adds fuel to the fire," said a Canadian mining analyst.

Bre-X has been embattled since tests by its partner Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc. on its Busang gold property indicated the deposit may contain "insignificant" amounts of gold. Freeport also cited "visual differences" between its gold findings and Bre-X's samples, which analysts have suggested may indicate tampering.
Over the weekend, Canadian newspapers said a study by Normet Pty Ltd., an Australian mining consultant, pointed to abnormalities in gold taken from Busang.

Normet said in a July 1996 report commissioned by Bre-X that the gold particles in its Busang samples were "mostly rounded" and typical of placer gold normally found in streams over riverbeds, the Northern Miner weekly newspaper said.
Analysts said the report added to rumors about tampering because the Busang site is mostly bedrock.
"We'd like to see what Bre-X's technical people think of the (Normet) report. They've had it since July 1996," the mining analyst said.
A story in Barron's investment newspaper on Monday quoted gold analyst John Doody as saying he believed management had failed to adequately defend its methods and estimates.
"(The selling) has got to be a reaction to the Barron's article," said another trader on Monday.
"It's trading as if U.S. people are selling it...Guys are just saying, 'Get me out,'" he added.
Bre-X Chief Executive David Walsh has vigorously denied that tampering could have occurred and promised an independent audit would prove the company's findings at Busang.
Bre-X has estimated the deposit contains 70.95 million ounces of gold, potentially the biggest in the world.
A Canadian mining consultant hired by Bre-X is conducting its own survey of Busang and is expected to report its results by late April or early May.
But Walsh also kept the rumor mill churning over the weekend with his own theory that an unidentified suitor was buying up shares in preparation for a hostile takeover bid.

"I was naive enough to think that a deposit of this size would be allowed to be developed without interference from big business. We should have been wiser in that regard and more on our guard," Walsh told the Calgary Herald newspaper.
Meanwhile, Bre-X's legal headaches worsened on Monday as another group of U.S. investors filed a class action lawsuit alleging the company and certain officials violated U.S. securities laws.
Bre-X now faces a total of seven class action lawsuits -- six in the United States and one in Canada.

"Among other things, plaintiffs claim that defendants misrepresented and concealed material facts concerning the gold reserve calculations reported for Bre-X's gold strike in Central Busang, Indonesia," law firms Abbey, Gardy & Squitieri, LLP and Appel, Chitwood & Harley said in a statement on Monday.
The other suits -- filed in cities ranging from San Francisco to Windsor, Ontario -- charge that Bre-X executives gave inflated projections about the size of gold deposits at Busang.

Separately, Canadian mining company Teck Corp issued a statement on Monday to refute market rumors that the Vancouver-based gold miner held shares in Bre-X. Teck held talks with Bre-X last year about participating in the project, but they were broken off.
